newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S., France drop moves to solve command row.
newsitem.headline: U.S., France drop moves to solve command row.

text.p: The U.S. and France have dropped attempts to resolve a long-running dispute over command of NATO's strategic southern flank, U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen told reporters on Thursday.

Paris had been pushing for command of NATO's southern flank, AFSOUTH, at Naples to be taken out of U.S. hands and given to a European and had clearly linked the issue to the wider one of whether it would reintegrate into NATO's military wing.

Cohen, briefing reporters on a plane taking him to a NATO ministers meeting in Brussels, said he believed the issue had been deferred following the election of a socialist government in France led by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.
"I think that as a result of the elections, much of that (AFsouth) discussion has simply been deferred. I'm not aware of any discussions recently," he said.

Washington had made clear it would not hand over the command which was also responsible for Sixth Fleet in the Mediterranean, but several compromises had been discussed to enable President Jacques Chirac to pursue his plans for closer alliance ties.
Cohen said the issue was settled: "Well from my perspective. AFSOUTH is under U.S. command."

The French socialists have been critical of Chirac's move, which would have seen France reenter military structures it left in 1966 in return for efforts to build a greater European dimension within an expanded NATO.

Independent analysts say France can no longer resolve the issue ahead of a summit in Madrid in July when NATO will invite some former communist enemies to join the alliance as part of efforts to transform NATO into a post-Cold War security body.
